topic: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD start

audits.title: P06 Driving up quality: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.standard: NICE QS33: QS2 seen in rheumatology within 3 weeks of referral; QS3 newly diagnosed RA offered short-term glucocorticoids and combination DMARDs within 6 weeks of referral
audits.setting: Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust rheumatology department, Preston

cycle1.period: First year of the NEIAA (dates not stated)
cycle1.result: 22 patients (8.9%) seen within 3 weeks of referral; 5 (7%) started DMARD within 6 weeks; mean wait 66 days (range 5-138) to be seen and diagnosed; 65 (90%) given bridging steroids; 65 (92%) started DMARDs.

audits.intervention: Process mapping and driver diagrams identified changes: primary care referral guidelines, more triage and new appointment capacity, simpler booking, text reminders, one-stop clinic with ultrasound, more drug education clinic capacity.
audits.other_findings: 246 patients recruited, 71 with confirmed RA; 3-month follow-up forms completed in 61 (86%). Further waits of about 50 days if sent for investigations and 25–39 days for drug education.
audits.citation: Loh J, Withers J, FIsh S, MacPhie E. P06 Driving up quality: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit. Rheumatology. 2020;59(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa111.005.

audits.title: P017 Out of outlier status: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.standard: NICE QS33: QS2 seen within 3 weeks of referral; QS3 RA started on DMARDs within 6 weeks of referral
audits.setting: Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust rheumatology department, Preston

cycle1.result: 10% of all patients seen within 3 weeks; 7% of RA cohort (n=77) started DMARD within 6 weeks.

audits.intervention: Primary care referral guidelines, prompts for RF/CCP requests and changed antibody report wording, more triage and new appointment capacity (extra consultant, upskilled ESP), simpler booking, more drug education and monitoring clinic capacity, signposting to NRAS.

cycle2.result: 54% seen within 3 weeks; 56% of RA cohort (n=73) started DMARD within 6 weeks.

audits.other_findings: Remission/low disease activity at 3 months rose from 54% (year 1) to 69% (year 2); baseline disease activity was lower in year 2.
audits.citation: MacPhie E, Ashcroft L, Brazendale J, Foreman N, Gilbert S, Greenall C, et al.. P017 Out of outlier status: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit. Rheumatology. 2021;60(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.016.

audits.title: P020 The impact of COVID-19: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.standard: NICE quality standard QS33 (QS2 and QS3: seen within 3 weeks of referral; DMARD started within 6 weeks)
audits.setting: Local rheumatology department submitting to the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit

cycle1.result: 54% of all patients seen within 3 weeks of referral; 56% of RA patients started DMARD within 6 weeks.

audits.intervention: No planned change; comparison during COVID-19 pandemic (face-to-face urgent clinics maintained)

cycle2.result: 41% of all patients seen within 3 weeks of referral; 58% of RA patients started DMARD within 6 weeks.

audits.other_findings: In year 3 patients had longer symptom duration before referral and higher disease activity at baseline and 3 months; 17 had telephone follow-up without DAS28.
audits.citation: . P020 The impact of COVID-19: local observations from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2022;61(Suppl 1).

audits.title: P100 Ethnic disparities in NICE rheumatoid arthritis quality standard 33 attainment: data from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit
audits.standard: NICE RA quality standard 33: QS1 referral within 3 working days of primary care presentation; QS2 conventional DMARD within 6 weeks of referral
audits.setting: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham rheumatology service, compared with national NEIAA data

cycle1.period: April 2018 to March 2024 (QEHB); May 2018 to March 2020 (national)
cycle1.result: QEHB QS1: 79% (115/146) White vs 21% (31/146) BAME referred within 3 days; QS2: 26.5% (27/102) BAME vs 73.5% (75/102) White. Nationally QS1 43% (12,561/29,417) White vs 47% (2,333/4,964) BAME; QS2 60% (723/1,204) BAME vs 57% (4,919/8,695) White.

audits.other_findings: 24% of QEHB patients were BAME vs 14% nationally; authors call for research into causes of ethnic disparities.
audits.citation: Shahnawaz Z, Nooh N, Budhwani A, Turkawi R, Filer A, Justice E, et al.. P100 Ethnic disparities in NICE rheumatoid arthritis quality standard 33 attainment: data from the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit. Rheumatology. 2026;65(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.135.

audits.title: The first national clinical audit for rheumatoid arthritis.
audits.standard: NICE quality standards for rheumatoid arthritis
audits.setting: Rheumatology services in the national audit for rheumatoid and early inflammatory arthritis

cycle1.period: First 3 months of follow-up from first presentation
cycle1.result: Delays in referral and access to specialist care, and need for improvement in treating to target, suppressing high disease activity and supporting self-care.

audits.other_findings: Patient-reported outcomes improved within 3 months with high satisfaction, but response rates were low.
audits.citation: Firth J, Snowden N, Ledingham J, Rivett A, Galloway J, Dennison EM, et al.. The first national clinical audit for rheumatoid arthritis. Br J Nurs. 2016;25(11):613-617. doi:10.12968/bjon.2016.25.11.613. PMID: 27281595.

audits.title: Patient- and clinician-reported outcomes for patients with new presentation of inflammatory arthritis: observations from the National Clinical Audit for Rheumatoid and Early Inflammatory Arthritis.
audits.setting: English and Welsh rheumatology units (National Clinical Audit for Rheumatoid and Early Inflammatory Arthritis)

cycle1.result: DAS28 calculated for 2659 (91%) RA patients at first assessment (mean 5.0); mean 3.5 after 3 months, slightly over 60% with meaningful reduction; 78% reported good experience; only 42% asked about work.

audits.title: Achievement of NICE quality standards for patients with new presentation of inflammatory arthritis: observations from the National Clinical Audit for Rheumatoid and Early Inflammatory Arthritis.
audits.standard: Six NICE quality standards for early inflammatory arthritis (e.g. GP referral within 3 days, specialist assessment within 3 weeks, DMARD within 6 weeks)
audits.setting: Rheumatology services in England and Wales (national audit)

cycle1.result: GP referral within 3 days 17%; specialist assessment within 3 weeks 38%; DMARD within 6 weeks in RA 53%; structured education within 1 month 59%; treatment target set 91%, achieved within 3 months 27%; helpline available in 96% of trusts.

audits.other_findings: 97% of trusts and health boards participated; substantial geographic variability; 36% received combination DMARDs and 82% steroids in the first 3 months.
audits.citation: Ledingham JM, Snowden N, Rivett A, Galloway J, Ide Z, Firth J, et al.. Achievement of NICE quality standards for patients with new presentation of inflammatory arthritis: observations from the National Clinical Audit for Rheumatoid and Early Inflammatory Arthritis. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2017;56(2):223-230. doi:10.1093/rheumatology/kew308. PMID: 27694337.

audits.title: Time to start disease modifying drugs for adults with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis: results of the first year of the national New Zealand Rheumatology Association (NZRA) audit.
audits.standard: Start DMARD within 6 weeks of referral

cycle1.result: 64.8% started DMARD within 6 weeks of referral

audits.other_findings: Time associated with rheumatologist FTE per 100,000 and rurality; 1.0 FTE/100,000 associated with 80% meeting target.
audits.citation: Taylor WJ, Dalbeth N, Kain T, White D, Grainger R, Quincey V.
